title: Hyperspectral + RGBD line scan
subtitle: SWIR line-scan camera + D435 over the belt
summary: The scan tunnel's two optical sensors over the conveyor: a 16-band SWIR (925-1675 nm) push-broom line-scan camera triggered by the belt encoder, and a D435 RGBD camera downstream. The description gives the line camera's lens, height and position, the vendor's per-band gain and dark level, and the D435's nominal intrinsics. Calibration finds where the scan line really falls on the belt and its lens scale, each band's radiometric gain and dark level from white / grey / black / dark references, and the D435's intrinsics, pose and depth scale and offset.

model.source: sysid's conveyor.xml + two MuJoCo cameras (the line camera's row is its centre row)

cameras.name: hsi_line
cameras.source: a 640-pixel SWIR push-broom line (Specim FX17 class): fx 900 px nominal

cameras.name: rgbd
cameras.source: a D435 at 640 x 480 (intel_rgbd: baseline 49.9 mm, depth unit 1 mm)

sensors.measures: 16-band DN per pixel per line; dot centres (pixel, belt position at the line)
belt travel; it triggers the line camera

known.note: band centres and widths are the vendor's (not identified here); the belt speed and encoder trigger come from the conveyor example; the target card's printed geometry and the references' reflectance are certified

target.risers_note: the D435 frames alternate the card flat on the belt and on a certified 150 mm riser: depth relief for its focal length, standoff and depth scale

coverage.function: sysid adapter: across-track bins (16 of the 640-pixel line) x the card's two heights
coverage.rule: share of the 32 (line bin, height) cells the planned dots fall in; the radiometric references cover every band at four levels

notes: Band centres and widths are the vendor's: identifying them needs a spectral lamp, not simulated.
The plastics are synthetic spectra shaped like the polymers' SWIR features, not library data.
Dot detections are simulated as exact crossings plus noise (no rendered line images, no detector in the loop).
